awd_titl_txt: Conference: 2025 Cal-Bridge Doctoral Scholars Summer Institute
awd_abstract_narration:
The University of California Irvine will organize and the University of California Santa Barbara will host the third Cal-Bridge Summer Institute Alumni Conference, July 20-26, 2025.  Participants will be doctoral students who are alumni of Cal-Bridge, a partnership between the University of California (UC) and the California State University (CSU) systems designed to provide pathways into research and the professorate for students from CSU and California community college campuses.  Participating scholars will form a peer learning community built on a community-of-practice model.  The summer program will focus on how people learn and effective learning strategies, along with facilitating teaching and learning.  The group will continue with regular virtual meetings throughout the academic year to promote the exchange of ideas and best practices. The portion of the workshop costs funded by the NSF will support funding for 25 Cal-Bridge Doctoral Scholars to participate in the Summer Institute.

The Cal-Bridge Summer Institute, a series of professional development workshops, will have two major thrusts: 1) developing effective pedagogues, and 2) developing effective research leaders. In addition to these, the conference will include a variety of shorter professional development mentorship sessions, and community and cohort building activities.  This conference aims to address two systemic points of loss along the professorial and professional researcher pathway for Cal-Bridge Alumni currently in PhD programs outside of the University of California system: completion of the PhD and entrance into the workforce.  Specifically, the award will: 1) Broaden the impact of the professional development being offered to a larger group of doctoral scholars, and 2) Provide space for Cal-Bridge Doctoral students to hold discussions and activities to build up their professional network and community.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
In July 2025 at the University of California, Santa Barbara, 47 Cal-Bridge Doctoral Scholars gathered for a week-long conference: the Third Cal-Bridge Summer  Institute (CB SI). This cohort consists of Ph.D. students in astronomy, physics, and computer  science from across the country, where 36 students were from University of California  campuses and 11 were from non-UC universities. This Conference Grant supported the expenses for the attendance of these Doctoral Scholars, all who are alumni from the Cal-Bridge Undergraduate Program and alumni from California State University campuses

Co-PIs Rodriguez Wimberly, Hood, and Callori attended the SI to facilitate 2.5 days of pedagogy workshops. PIIs Rudolph and Schumm attended the SI in their leadership roles, facilitating fruitful discussions with the scholars regarding the evolution of the Cal-Bridge program. PI Rodriguez Wimberly and senior graduate student Justin Bracks led multiple workshops on community building, networking, and peer mentorship. The consultancy group Vitae UK led research leadership workshops. 

The week-long conference provided Doctoral Scholars in two cohorts a variety of professional development activities centered around effective pedagogy and development of research skills to prepare them to become research leaders in their fields. The pedagogy training included (1) 1 full day of dedicated network building activities; (2) 2.5 full days of pedagogy workshops, where topics included (a) "How People Learn", (b) active learning techniques, and (c) backwards design. The research focused professional development included topics included (a) research skills development (including technical and social skills), and (b) team management. Two community building events were also hosted during the week. 

This third Summer Institute fully solidified the importance of community gathering, in-person learning and collaboration - as was initially felt in the first two SIs. As many members in this first Cal-Bridge Doctoral Scholar cohort become senior graduate students and thus begin to transition into next career stages, this SI proved critical for career mentorship - in both peers sharing resources, learned experiences, and opportunities and program leadership advising on these next steps. This incredibly successful and fulfilling weeklong conference culminated in a morning of action as alumni gathered to brainstorm and create action plans to continue to build and support the growing Cal-Bridge Alumni network. We each recognize the incredible program and support structures that the Cal-Bridge undergraduate program has afforded us and are determined to continue the paths we are creating not only for ourselves but also for the students coming up behind us.
